description: A single-panel table rendered as an image (Table 2, "Mechanical properties at RT and LNT") with seven columns and two data rows; no plots, micrographs or schematic elements are present. The column headers, exactly as printed, are: "Test temperature", "Ultimate tensile strength, MPa", "Yield strength, MPa", "Uniform elongation, %", "Total elongation, %", "Reduction of area, %" and "CVN impact energy, J". The two test-temperature rows are labelled "RT" (room temperature) and "LNT" (liquid nitrogen temperature). For RT the tabulated values are 580 ± 6 MPa ultimate tensile strength, 251 ± 3 MPa yield strength, 38.5 ± 0.5 % uniform elongation, 52.0 ± 0.5 % total elongation, 78 ± 0.5 % reduction of area and 331 ± 4 J CVN impact energy. For LNT the values are 945 ± 8 MPa ultimate tensile strength, 497 ± 5 MPa yield strength, 56.0 ± 0.5 % uniform elongation, 75.5 ± 0.5 % total elongation, 80 ± 1 % reduction of area and 254 ± 6 J CVN impact energy. The table therefore shows that cooling from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperature roughly doubles strength (UTS 580 → 945 MPa, YS 251 → 497 MPa), increases both uniform and total elongation (38.5 → 56.0 % and 52.0 → 75.5 %), slightly raises reduction of area (78 → 80 %), and lowers Charpy impact energy (331 → 254 J) while retaining a high toughness value. All values carry ± standard deviations; no error bars or replicate counts are shown.

observations.observation: The figure is a two-row data table whose row labels are the test temperatures 'RT' and 'LNT' (room temperature and liquid nitrogen temperature).

The table reports six mechanical-property columns with the printed headers: 'Ultimate tensile strength, MPa', 'Yield strength, MPa', 'Uniform elongation, %', 'Total elongation, %', 'Reduction of area, %' and 'CVN impact energy, J'.
At RT the table lists UTS 580 ± 6 MPa, YS 251 ± 3 MPa, uniform elongation 38.5 ± 0.5 %, total elongation 52.0 ± 0.5 %, reduction of area 78 ± 0.5 % and CVN impact energy 331 ± 4 J.
At LNT the table lists UTS 945 ± 8 MPa, YS 497 ± 5 MPa, uniform elongation 56.0 ± 0.5 %, total elongation 75.5 ± 0.5 %, reduction of area 80 ± 1 % and CVN impact energy 254 ± 6 J.
Every tabulated entry is given as a mean with a ± deviation; no replicate number or test standard is printed in the table.
The caption states the table gives mechanical properties at RT and LNT.

The citing text states the 0.2 % offset yield strength (YS) increases from 251 to 497 MPa and the UTS increases from 580 MPa to 945 MPa as temperature decreases from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperature.
The citing text states the low temperature raises uniform elongation (UEL) from 38.5 % to 56.0 % and total elongation (TEL) from 52.0 % to 75.5 %.

The citing text states the Charpy V-notch (CVN) impact energy is 331 ± 4 J at room temperature and 254 ± 6 J at cryogenic temperature, indicating excellent toughness at both RT and LNT for the low-carbon low-density steel.

The citing text states that the strength-ductility trade-off is evaded via low temperature, since both strength and ductility at -196 °C exceed those at room temperature; the table itself shows the same trends numerically.

The table shows that strength and elongation increase at LNT while CVN impact energy decreases from 331 J (RT) to 254 J (LNT), i.e. a strength-toughness trade-off accompanies the strength-ductility gain.
The citing text mentions Fig. 2 (a) as the source of engineering stress-strain curves at 20 °C and -196 °C; those curves are not part of this table image.
